name: Religious-Nationalists
summary: Iran's Religious-Nationalists (melli-mazhabi) combine Iranian nationalism in the tradition of Mosaddegh with a modernist reading of Islam, holding that Islam and democracy can coexist. They seek constitutional, accountable government through peaceful reform, reject both royal and clerical dictatorship including Guardianship of the Islamic Jurist, and want political life guided by religious values without clerical rule. Their economics range from Islamic socialism to market liberalism.
scope: The Iranian current led by Mehdi Bazargan, Mahmoud Taleghani and the Freedom Movement of Iran (founded 1961), descended from the religious wing of Mosaddegh's National Front, and the Council of Nationalist-Religious Activists. It does not cover religious nationalism in general (Hindutva, Christian nationalism, Sinhalese Buddhist nationalism and so on), which have separate entries. The sources say little about sharia, gender and social issues, so many answers are low-confidence inferences.

sources.title: Religious-Nationalists (Wikipedia)
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Definition of the Iranian faction, its two pillars, reformism, non-violence, internal economic diversity and its stance on clerical rule.

sources.title: Freedom Movement of Iran (Wikipedia)
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Platform of the movement's main organisation: rejection of royal and clerical dictatorship, constitution, Universal Declaration of Human Rights, sovereignty, liberalism.

sources.title: The Freedom Movement of Iran
sources.author: Iran Data Portal, Syracuse University
sources.usedFor: Founding principles: separation of mosque and state with religious values guiding politics, constitutional monarchy, neutrality, rejection of state interventionism, liberal reading of Islam.

sources.title: Mehdi Bazargan (Wikipedia)
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Bazargan's views as the camp's central figure: Islamic Democratic Republic, opposition to the clergy-written constitution, Gandhi, opposition to the Iraq war.

sources.title: Opposition group calls for boycott of elections (report of a Freedom Movement statement)
sources.author: Radio Zamaneh, 24 February 2012
sources.usedFor: A Freedom Movement statement as reported: demand for free elections and denunciation of the establishment's totalitarianism. A news report of the statement, not its full text.

sources.title: A voice against vengeance (reports Bazargan's public statement)
sources.author: Christian Science Monitor, 9 October 1981
sources.usedFor: Bazargan's quoted warning that acts of revenge would turn the country into an ocean of blood, and his condemnation of daily executions.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The movement rejects royal dictatorship, but titles are not specifically addressed.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: A devout Muslim camp would keep marriage as a legal institution.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: A movement favouring liberal economics and rejecting state interventionism does not seek to abolish money or wage labour.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Contrary to a constitutionalist movement seeking rule of law.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: National sovereignty and the UN Charter in the platform fit this, though not specifically addressed.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The movement opposes clerical dictatorship, supports a liberal reading of Islam and the Universal Declaration.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: The camp is strictly non-violent and values neutrality.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Immigration and assimilation are absent from the sources on this Iranian faction.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The movement itself was disqualified from elections, which leaves it hostile to party bans.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The movement stands for constitutional limits on rulers, and parliamentary control of the purse is basic to that.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: The movement wants constitutional, accountable government and rejects personal or clerical dictatorship, so a leader bypassing parties and groups is opposed.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about imperialism, and the statement now asks only whether capitalism inevitably causes wars between great powers.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Religious values guide the camp but freedom of expression is a platform item.

central-planning.rationale: The Freedom Movement rejects state interventionism, so central planning is contrary to its economic stance.

church-by-bishops.rationale: A Christian-specific question; no relevance to this movement.

civilizational-union.rationale: The camp is Iranian-nationalist and rejects Pan-Islamism, according to Wikipedia, so uniting nations of one civilization is not its aim.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Mosaddeghist anti-colonial heritage; contrary to national sovereignty.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Religious nationalists favour social justice but reject Marxist historical materialism, although Islamic socialists in the camp lean its way.

clerical-rule.rationale: The Freedom Movement rejects clerical dictatorship and Guardianship of the Islamic Jurist, and Bazargan resigned over clerical privileges.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Platform emphasises sovereignty and UN Charter.

collective-defense.rationale: Neutrality favours no, but the camp sought accommodation with the West.

communal-electorates.rationale: Contrary to equal civic rights and democratic ideals.

consent-of-governed.rationale: A pro-democracy constitutionalist party whose platform demands free elections and respect for the constitution.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Bazargan supported the original revolutionary draft constitution and opposed the Assembly of Experts that rewrote it, which favours a broadly representative drafting body.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognised bodies setting wages and prices conflicts with the movement's rejection of state interventionism.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: A constitutionalist movement that demands respect for the constitution accepts limits on majorities.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: The question concerns African customary chiefs and has no bearing here.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: No tax policy is documented and the economic wing ranges from socialist to liberal, so adherents are split.

democracy-best.rationale: The faction argues that Islam and democracy can coexist and seeks democracy through reform, making democracy its central goal.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The movement champions free competitive elections as the core of democracy, but also demands constitutional limits.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The movement rejects dictatorship of any kind.

direct-action.rationale: The movement pursued reform through elections and parliament; its early civil disobedience was aimed at restoring constitutional government, not replacing elections.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Contrary to human rights principles in the platform.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Social justice under Islam is a stated goal, but needs-based distribution is not specified.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Authority and religion are linked by religious values, but Wikipedia says they seek democracy and the Freedom Movement separates mosque and state, so authority rests on the people.

dominated-front.rationale: Mosaddeghist anti-imperialism points yes, but Bazargan sought accommodation with the West and the camp stayed neutral.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The platform upholds the Universal Declaration of Human Rights and individual freedoms, so duties do not outrank rights.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The movement rejects royal dictatorship and demands elections.

elective-rulers.rationale: The movement demands free elections and rejects royal rule.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Bazargan condemned mass executions of regime opponents and repression, and the platform upholds rights.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its rationale is about other international bodies (such as the EU, WTO, IMF or WHO) or about support, funding or reform without enforcement powers, and the statement now asks whether the UN should have powers to enforce its decisions against member states.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The movement favours international neutrality and independence.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The platform calls for respect for the constitution and the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The platform supports the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Social justice under Islam is in the platform, but equality of outcome is not specified.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The camp is committed to the vote and reform within the country; exit is not valued over democracy.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: The movement stands for peaceful, accountable, constitutional government, and Bazargan publicly spoke against revolutionary vengeance and summary executions.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Their economics are documented as ranging from Islamic socialism to market liberalism, so adherents are split and no position on this tax is recorded.

force-without-un.rationale: Respect for the UN Charter in the platform weighs against unilateral force.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Nationalist sovereignty points yes, economic liberalism no, and the sources do not decide.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Platform commits to Universal Declaration of Human Rights.

gradual-change.rationale: The sources describe the camp as favouring reform over revolution and gradual sociopolitical change.

harm-principle.rationale: Liberal in outlook but religious values guide public life, so a pure harm principle is not clearly theirs.

head-commands-forces.rationale: A constitutionalist party favouring parliamentary checks would not centre command in the head of state.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Contrary to the human rights commitments in the platform.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Iranianness and Islamicness are the camp's pillars.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Mosaddeghism tied independence to oil nationalisation, but the movement's economics are mixed.

independent-unions.rationale: The camp stands for freedom of association and rejects state control of civil society.

indirect-election.rationale: Direct elections are central to the movement's democratic demand.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Economic liberalism leans yes but nothing is documented.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The platform backs the Universal Declaration, but a religious-nationalist group would also recognise communal identity.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: A modernist camp that holds religion and modernity compatible would not call industrial civilization a disaster.

informal-organisation.rationale: The movement is a formal political party seeking reform.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: The movement calls the Islamic Republic totalitarian and demands free expression and free elections, so cutting internet access to maintain order runs against its platform.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: National sovereignty is a stated principle of the platform.

islam-incompatible.rationale: The camp's founding claim is that Islam and democracy and modernity coexist.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Wikipedia distinguishes the camp from Pan-Islamism and it is Iranian-nationalist.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Marxist thesis foreign to the camp.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Their economics range from Islamic socialism to liberalism, so the strands are split on this.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Wikipedia distinguishes the camp from Pan-Islamism, and its nationalism is Iranian and tied to Islam rather than purely language.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Bazargan preferred an Islamic Democratic Republic with a non-theocratic constitution, so laws drawn simply from scripture do not match his view.

leader-cult.rationale: It rejects royal and clerical dictatorship, whose leaders are the objects of such cults.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The camp itself spans left and right, but no statement exists.

limit-population.rationale: The sources on the camp never discuss population policy, and religious values and modernist development goals point different ways.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalisation rules do not appear in the sources on the camp.

majority-settlement.rationale: Contrary to equal rights in the Universal Declaration.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The Iran Data Portal says the Freedom Movement rejects state interventionism and Wikipedia says it favours economic liberalism, pointing to trust in markets over officials.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Not Marxist; religion and ideas matter for them.

means-match-ends.rationale: Bazargan admired Gandhi and the movement is strictly non-violent, matching methods to democratic ends.

military-guardian-role.rationale: A constitutionalist party that rejects dictatorship opposes a political role for the armed forces.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Contrary to the Universal Declaration commitment and the movement's liberal reading of Islam.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The Freedom Movement's founders backed a constitutional monarchy limited by the constitution (s3), but they later turned against the Shah and supported the revolution, so the agreement is weak.

nation-first.rationale: The platform pairs national sovereignty with respect for the UN Charter, so it does not clearly rank national interest above cooperation.

national-church-status.rationale: The movement opposed constitutional clerical privilege and separates mosque and state.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The platform explicitly respects the UN Charter and international human rights norms.

national-mission.rationale: Its principles are national sovereignty and neutrality, not exporting a government model.

national-rebirth.rationale: The camp seeks democratic renewal but does not frame it as decadence needing radical rebirth.

national-resource-control.rationale: Mosaddeghism, which the camp claims to continue, centred on national sovereignty over oil, and the platform advocates national sovereignty.

national-self-determination.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its rationale rests on the sovereignty of existing countries, and the statement now asks whether every people that sees itself as a nation has the right to a state of its own.

natural-rulers.rationale: The movement rejects royal and clerical dictatorship, which rest on claims that some are born or trained to rule.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The camp's Islamic socialists and liberals would answer differently.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Strict nonviolence concerns political methods, not self-defence, which Islam permits.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Rejects state interventionism but also puts social justice in the platform, so a minimal state is going too far.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: The sources on the camp do not discuss territorial compromise.

one-party-rule.rationale: The Freedom Movement is a pro-democracy party that rejects dictatorship, and it has itself been excluded by a ruling establishment.

organic-representation.rationale: The movement wants a constitutional parliamentary democracy with parties; it is a political party itself.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The movement backed a constitutional monarchy whose power was limited by the constitution, implying legislative supremacy.

party-controls-media.rationale: Freedom of expression is a platform item.

party-own-road.rationale: A communist-movement question with no bearing on this camp.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Their nationalism is paired with concern for the people's welfare and accountable government, though workers are not singled out.

person-over-state.rationale: Support for the Universal Declaration and constitutional limits puts the person above the state.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about one government, party or regime, or about fighting corruption, not a general claim that most politicians put their own interests first, which this statement now asks.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: National sovereignty is a stated platform item.

population-transfer.rationale: Contrary to the Universal Declaration commitment.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The camp rests on two pillars, Iranianness and Islamicness, so preserving national culture and tradition is central.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Rejection of state interventionism points no, social justice points yes.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Social justice under Islam is part of the platform.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The movement stands for constitutional state institutions under law; privatised courts and defence are far from its liberalism.

production-for-use.rationale: The camp's Islamic socialists might agree while liberals would not.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Economic liberals in the camp accept profit as legitimate; Islamic socialists might not.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Respect for the constitution and the rule of law is central to its constitutionalism.

property-fundamental.rationale: Economic liberals and Islamic socialists coexist in the camp, so no firm line on property rights can be drawn from the sources.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Freedom of expression and political activity, and criticism of secrecy under the regime, support open information.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Its liberal reading of Islam and defence of free expression oppose state punishment of blasphemy.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The platform upholds the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The camp holds that religion and modernity coexist; it does not make reason the only guide.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: The faction's modernist religious outlook says religion and modernism coexist, which requires reinterpretation.

religion-illusion.rationale: A religious movement guided by religious values.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: The movement is religious and holds that religion and modernity coexist.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The movement opposed constitutional articles granting special clerical rights and rejected Guardianship of the Islamic Jurist, favouring equal standing among interpretations.

religious-nation.rationale: The faction rests on both Iranianness and Islamicness, but Wikipedia says it favours democracy compatible with Islam, not defining the nation purely by religion.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The movement's early civil disobedience aimed to press the Shah to restore constitutional rule, although it stopped short of violence.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Economics range from Islamic socialism to market liberalism, so adherents are split on common ownership of resources.

restore-past-order.rationale: The camp is modernist and reformist, aiming at democratic progress rather than restoring a lost order.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Political freedom is core to its platform.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Freedom of expression is in the platform, but modernist Muslims may accept limits on incitement; the sources are silent on hate speech.

return-to-foraging.rationale: A modernist movement that reconciles religion and modernity has no use for primitivism.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The Iranian camp has no documented claim of a nation divided by outside borders.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The camp rests on Iranian and Islamic heritage as pillars.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Bazargan was a modernist who reinterpreted religion in light of science, not a literalist.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Bazargan condemned the regime's executions and warned that revenge would turn the country into an ocean of blood, indicating support for accountability for abuses.

separate-church-state.rationale: The Freedom Movement says it believes in separating mosque and state while holding that political activity should be guided by religious values, so a strict separation is not what it asks.

separated-powers.rationale: Constitutionalism and respect for the constitution are core to its identity as a Constitutionalist party.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The faction pursues democracy through reform rather than revolution.

social-market-economy.rationale: Social justice combined with economic liberalism and competition matches this model.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Not relevant to a non-Marxist camp.

socialized-markets.rationale: The camp includes Islamic socialists who might accept it and liberals who would not.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The movement is Constitutionalist and demands respect for the constitution.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: A constitutionalist movement accepts state monopoly of arms and rejects armed groups.

state-as-business.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its value turns on whether citizens are customers who can leave, and the statement now asks only whether government should be run on business principles.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Rejection of state interventionism means the Freedom Movement does not favour the state steering investment.

state-harmful.rationale: The movement is constitutionalist and wants a democratic state under law; it never questions the state's necessity.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: A religious movement guided by religious values.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The Freedom Movement favours international neutrality and independence, per the Iran Data Portal.

strong-leader.rationale: The Freedom Movement rejects both royal and clerical dictatorship and stands for constitutionalism, so bypassing institutions through a strong leader runs against its core.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The movement separates mosque and state and opposed constitutional articles granting special clerical rights.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The movement rejects dictatorship and has itself been suppressed.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The platform stresses civil liberties and freedom of political activity and expression, which weighs against broad surveillance; no direct statement exists.

taxation-theft.rationale: A constitutionalist movement that seeks social justice accepts the legitimacy of taxation.

territorial-expansion.rationale: National sovereignty and international neutrality are its principles, and it opposed prolonging the Iraq war.

total-state.rationale: It rejects dictatorship and state interventionism and campaigns for civil liberties.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Drilled youth movements are a tool of dictatorships, which the movement rejects.

unions-good.rationale: Left-leaning members are social democrats; support for unions follows from social-justice concerns, but nothing in the sources says so directly.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Strictly non-violent and rejects clerical claims of legitimacy.

war-builds-character.rationale: Bazargan opposed continuing the Iran-Iraq War after 1982 and the movement sought its early end.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The movement is a political party that has campaigned for decades.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Women's rights are barely covered in the sources on this camp, and its left and liberal wings would answer differently.

women-suffrage.rationale: The Universal Declaration commitment and the camp's women's society support equal political rights.

workers-councils.rationale: A liberal, constitutionalist movement does not look to workers' councils in place of parliaments.

missingStatements.text: Political activity should be guided by religious values, but clergy should hold no special political power.
missingStatements.rationale: This is the Freedom Movement's founding formula: it separates mosque and state yet wants religious values to guide politics, and it opposed constitutional articles granting the clergy special rights.

missingStatements.text: Rule by a senior religious jurist is illegitimate.
missingStatements.rationale: The movement rejects Guardianship of the Islamic Jurist, and Bazargan's government resigned over clerical privileges.

missingStatements.text: A country's natural resources should be under national rather than foreign control.
missingStatements.rationale: Mosaddeghism, which the camp claims to continue, centred on national sovereignty over oil, and the platform advocates national sovereignty.

notes: The camp is internally diverse: some members are Islamic socialists, others economic liberals. Primary text is scarce online: the only direct quotation used is from a news report, and the Freedom Movement item is a news report of its statement. Many low-confidence zeros reflect that the sources do not address the topic. The Wikipedia article on the faction says its hopes of being accepted as loyal opposition have not been met.
